definitions.explanation: A hand game played between two or more people using three hand shapes: rock (fist), paper (flat hand), and scissors (two fingers extended). Rock beats scissors, scissors beats paper, and paper beats rock.

examples.japanese: じゃんけんで{順番|じゅんばん}を{決|き}めよう。
examples.english: Let's decide the order with rock-paper-scissors.

examples.japanese: じゃんけんで{負|ま}けたから、{掃除|そうじ}{当番|とうばん}になった。
examples.english: I lost at rock-paper-scissors, so I became the cleaning duty person.

examples.japanese: じゃんけんぽん！あいこでしょ！
examples.english: Rock, paper, scissors, shoot! It's a tie!
examples.notes: The standard chant used when playing

notes:
THE THREE HANDS:
・グー (rock/fist) - beats チョキ
・チョキ (scissors/peace sign) - beats パー
・パー (paper/flat hand) - beats グー

PLAYING PHRASES:
・じゃんけんぽん！ (Rock, paper, scissors, shoot!)
・あいこでしょ！ (It's a tie! - said when replaying after a draw)
・{最初|さいしょ}はグー！ (First is rock! - optional starting phrase)

COMMON USES IN JAPAN:
・Deciding who goes first in games
・Settling disputes fairly among friends
・Choosing who pays for a meal ({割|わ}り{勘|かん} situations)
・Children's games and classroom activities

VARIATIONS:
・{後出|あとだ}しじゃんけん (delayed rock-paper-scissors - cheating)
・{連続|れんぞく}じゃんけん (continuous/tournament style)

COLLOCATIONS:
・じゃんけんで{決|き}める (to decide by rock-paper-scissors)
・じゃんけんに{勝|か}つ (to win at rock-paper-scissors)
・じゃんけんに{負|ま}ける (to lose at rock-paper-scissors)
・じゃんけんをする (to play rock-paper-scissors)
